title: Idle display fabs print stacked oxide-TFT memory panels
idea: Gen-8.5 LCD/OLED fabs (2.2 x 2.5 m glass, 1.5-2 um lithography, mature IGZO TFT know-how) sit in overcapacity. Retool them to build 4-8 BEOL-stacked oxide-TFT gain-cell memory layers on glass panels, dice panels into tiles, and attach them through a CXL controller as a ~100-300 ns capacity tier.
why: One panel has ~75x the area of a 300 mm wafer; at 2 um rules and 6 stacked layers that is ~100+ GB per panel on depreciated tools with no EUV, crystal growth or quartz crucibles, potentially undercutting 4x-inflated DRAM $/GB for capacity tiers.

title: Stranded-memory exchange: CXL fabric rents idle DRAM across racks
idea: Inverts 'memory belongs to one server': a row-scale CXL 3 memory fabric plus a spot-market scheduler leases the ~25-35% of installed DRAM that sits stranded to other servers by the minute, with prices that steer tenants.
why: Raises usable supply ~20-30% with no new wafers, offsetting the 4x price spike; materials per useful bit fall by the same factor.

title: Hydrogen-terminated diamond access transistor doped by vanadium oxide
idea: TRIZ #35 Parameter change (raise the bandgap from 1.1 to 5.5 eV): grow nanocrystalline diamond at <=500 C, hydrogen-terminate it, and cap it with V2O5, whose deep electron affinity pulls a 2D hole gas into the surface (surface-transfer doping), sealed under Al2O3. The channel needs no dopants and its off-state leakage is negligible.
why: Attacks the <=13 fA leakage tail that forces refresh (fact 3). Retention could stretch from 64 ms to seconds or more, cutting refresh energy (16-33% of idle power) by >90%, using only C, H, V, Al and O.

title: Nested conductive-core insulating-shell nanograins give colossal effective k
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: build the dielectric from ~3 nm semiconducting reduced-TiO2 grains, each wrapped by ALD in a 0.5 nm Al2O3 shell. The field drops only across the thin shells (an engineered version of CaCu3Ti4O12's internal barrier layers), so effective k could reach several hundred.
why: Targets fact 1's k ~70 requirement with Ti, Al and O only. The risk is that Maxwell-Wagner relaxation is too slow for ns access and that leakage percolates through the cores.

title: Single carbon nanotubes coated as 1-micron coaxial storage capacitors
idea: Coaxial capacitance per length is 2*pi*eps/ln(r2/r1): a 1 nm-radius nanotube with 2 nm ZrO2 and a TiN shell gives ~2 fF/um, so a 1 um tube suffices at 10 nm pitch. Grow vertical tubes by methane CVD from Fe catalyst dots on each vertical-transistor drain.
why: ~100 nm2/cell vs 864 = ~9-10x density with an AR-100 pillar that is grown rather than etched (no fluorocarbon HAR etch), from carbon and iron. Catalyst contamination and tube placement are the risks.

title: Polysilicon plant SiCl4 waste becomes synthetic silica crucible liners
idea: Combine the Siemens polysilicon byproduct stream with crucible making: flame-hydrolyze waste SiCl4 into ultra-pure synthetic silica soot, fuse it as the melt-contacting 3-5 mm inner layer, and build the outer bubble-composite body from ordinary quartz sand.
why: Breaks the Spruce Pine >80% high-purity-quartz chokepoint by turning a waste (~10+ kg SiCl4 per kg poly) into the scarce input, sited at U.S. polysilicon plants.

title: Turbogenerator hydrogen cooling replaces helium as electrostatic-chuck backside gas
idea: Large power-plant generators are cooled with hydrogen because its thermal conductivity (~0.18 W/m-K) beats helium (~0.15). Use onsite PEM-electrolysis H2, or a sub-flammable H2/N2 blend at the ~10 Torr backside pressure, as the wafer-to-chuck heat-transfer gas in etch and CVD chucks, treating the small leak into the plasma as a known minor process species.
why: Removes the largest single helium use in a DRAM fab with equal or better wafer temperature control during high-aspect-ratio capacitor etch; ~100% helium substitution for chuck cooling using gas makeable anywhere in the U.S.

title: KOH-on-(110)-silicon crystal-plane trenches for capacitor fins
idea: Periodic-table walk, K (19): on (110) wafers, alkaline etchants cut near-perfect vertical {111} walls at 100-600:1 plane selectivity, so one DUV line mask along <112> yields atomically smooth deep trench/fin capacitors; TMAH substitutes for KOH where alkali contamination matters.
why: Swaps EUV-pitch plasma HAR etch for wet crystal anisotropy, fluorine-free, at roughly 1/20 the etch-tool capital.

title: Test in the field, not on the tester: self-learned error maps
idea: Reverse when testing happens: ship dies after minimal wafer sort, and let on-die BIST plus ECC syndrome logging build and update the bad-cell map during normal use, within the 1% BER budget.
why: ATE capital and test energy are a large back-end cost; cuts test time per die ~5-10x and removes burn-in ovens.

title: Jam jar: precursor ampoule heel recovery and repurification service
idea: Stimulus 'jam jar' (the last scrape left in the jar) -> a 10-person team collects returned ALD/CVD ampoules still holding 10-25% unused Hf, Zr, Ru or Mo precursor heel, fractionally sublimes or distills it to spec and refills the ampoules.
why: Recovers scarce-metal precursors otherwise incinerated; cuts precursor demand ~15-20%.

title: Fiber-drawn salami capacitor arrays sliced into wafers
idea: Imposed scarcity: no lithography and no high-AR etch. Assemble a glass preform of millimetre metal-cored, glass-clad coaxial rods, thermally draw and restack-redraw it (as photonic-crystal fiber makers do) until cores reach ~50 nm pitch, then slice the fused bundle into 5 um discs and hybrid-bond them to a CMOS access-transistor wafer.
why: Feature size comes from draw ratio, not EUV; each slice is a sheet of billions of coaxial capacitors with AR ~100 at no etch cost, made from glass and common metals.

title: Space-shower mist rinse: megasonic aerosol rinses with one-tenth the water
idea: Astronauts wash with mist and no-rinse methods because water is precious. Replace overflow-bath rinses with megasonic-atomized UPW mist and an in-line resistivity endpoint that stops rinsing when the drain returns to 18 MOhm-cm, prototyped on a university spin-rinse-dryer.
why: Rinsing is most of a fab's UPW use; endpoint-controlled mist rinsing could cut rinse water ~70-90%.

title: NRAM revived with chlorine-purified methane nanotubes: a metal-free carbon cell
idea: Nantero NRAM stalled largely because CNT fabrics carried Fe/Co/Ni catalyst residue that DRAM fabs refused, and supply was boutique. Grow nanotubes by methane pyrolysis on a floating catalyst (co-producing hydrogen), strip metals to sub-ppb by ~2,500 C chlorine-gas purification as used for nuclear graphite, then spin the fabric as a two-terminal van der Waals switch between TiN electrodes in a crosspoint.
why: Switching element is pure carbon from natural gas (no Hf, Ge, Te, Pt), and the by-product H2 offsets fab energy; NRAM's ns-class switching, >1e11 cycles and nonvolatility remove capacitor and refresh; 4F2 crosspoint per deck.

title: Glass-cullet recycling turns spent fab quartzware into crucible feedstock
idea: Adapted from glassmakers' cullet remelting. Collect retired diffusion tubes, wafer boats, etch rings and bell jars (all made from HPQ fused silica), plasma-melt them, strip surface metals with chlorine-gas refining, and refuse the result into crucible inner-layer sand.
why: Recovers HPQ that was already mined at Spruce Pine. Fabs scrap tonnes of quartzware each year, so this cuts new HPQ demand ~10-20%.

title: Synthetic crucibles from polysilicon-plant tetrachloride waste
idea: Imposed scarcity: no natural high-purity quartz. Take the SiCl4 byproduct that Siemens polysilicon plants make (~3-4 kg per kg of poly), flame-hydrolyze it into silica soot as optical-fiber preform makers do, and press and sinter the soot into whole crucibles (not just inner liners) next to U.S. poly plants.
why: Turns a waste stream into a domestic HPQ substitute and decouples crucibles from one North Carolina deposit; low-alkali synthetic silica can raise crucible life and ingot yield ~10-20%.

title: Eliminate ingots and wire saws: kerfless seeded direct-solidified wafers
idea: Freeze 300 mm wafers directly from a silicon melt onto a cooled, seeded template that imposes single-crystal orientation, then high-temperature anneal to drive out dislocations; there is no ingot, no wire saw and no kerf.
why: Kerf wastes ~40% of polysilicon and ingot pulling is energy- and crucible-intensive; halves silicon and energy per wafer if defect density reaches DRAM grade.

title: Copper buried wordlines with self-forming manganese silicate barrier
idea: Worsen: fill every buried wordline, plug and contact with CVD tungsten from Chinese ore via WF6. Flip: fill the buried-channel wordline trench with electroplated Cu-Mn alloy that anneals into a self-forming MnSiOx barrier a few nm thick, capped with graphene against electromigration, so neither W nor a thick TiN liner is needed.
why: Tungsten (~80% China) and WF6 fluorine: Cu has ~3x lower bulk resistivity, so wordlines can be shallower or thinner, which also reduces gate-induced leakage; aim is W-free arrays.

title: Barrierless molybdenum contacts silicide themselves during the fill anneal
idea: Combine contact barrier, fill and silicide into one ALD Mo step from a fluorine-free chloride precursor (MoO2Cl2): Mo deposits directly on Si and a ~600 C anneal forms a MoSi2 interface, deleting the Ti/TiN liner and WF6 tungsten fill.
why: Tungsten-free and fluorine-free contacts; 20-40% lower contact resistance because no barrier eats the narrow via; Mo is U.S.-mined.

title: Reed-relay access DRAM: NEMS switches with zero off-leakage
idea: Revive the reed relays of the 1965 Bell No.1 ESS as BEOL NEMS contact switches that connect each storage capacitor to its bitline. When the switch is open, an air gap gives effectively zero leakage, so a small planar MIM capacitor holds charge for hours.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): refresh nearly disappears, so the capacitor can shrink to ~1 fF in flat MIM instead of high-aspect-ratio pillars (fact 1); BEOL at DUV pitch with no EUV; TiN/SiC materials, no Hf.

title: Seashell: calcium titanate capacitor dielectric from two abundant elements
idea: Stimulus 'seashell' (calcium carbonate) -> make the capacitor dielectric from calcium, the 5th most abundant element: ALD CaTiO3 (k ~150-180) with Al-doped grain boundaries, crystallized at low temperature on a seed layer between TiN or MoN electrodes.
why: Reaches the k >= 70 needed to beat the capacitor charge wall without hafnium, zirconium, strontium or ruthenium; Ca and Ti are geologically unlimited.

title: Calcium titanate perovskite capacitors from earth-abundant elements
idea: Box [CaTiO3 (k~150) cap | Si access | voltage SA | pillar | Si | thermal ALD from a Ca cyclopentadienyl + Ti amide + O3 with N2 purges]: grow perovskite CaTiO3 on a conductive Nb:TiO2 bottom electrode that seeds crystallization near 450 C, with no Sr, Ru or Hf.
why: Capacitor charge wall (needs k~70) and scarce-element intensity: Ca and Ti are abundant and US-available, and k~150 lets AR fall to ~25:1; crystallization temperature and leakage are the risks.

title: HBM die thinning by layer splitting so parent wafers recycle
idea: Combine HBM's mandatory 30-50 um die thinning with porous-silicon layer transfer: build core dies on epi above a buried porous-Si cleave plane, split the 40 um device layer off after carrier bonding instead of grinding ~700 um to slurry, then re-polish and re-epi the parent for 10+ reuses.
why: HBM grinds ~95% of each wafer's silicon away; reuse cuts prime wafer, polysilicon and crucible demand per HBM bit ~80-90% and removes grinding water.

title: Fe/Cr/Fe exchange stack builds cobalt- and ruthenium-free MRAM
idea: TRIZ #26 Copying the original 1988 GMR system: use Fe/Cr/Fe RKKY coupling as the synthetic antiferromagnet in place of Co/Ru/Co, and an Fe(001)/MgO(001)/Fe coherent-tunneling junction with interface perpendicular anisotropy. Mn-N pinning and TiN seed layers replace Ta, W and Pt.
why: STT-MRAM gives ~10-30 ns, refresh-free memory with ~1e12+ endurance, built only from Fe, Cr, Mn, Mg, Ti, N and O. A U.S. line would carry no Co, Ru, Ta, W or Pt exposure.

title: Spatial ALD converts precursor pulses in time into zones in space
idea: Time-to-space shift: rather than seconds-long pulse/purge cycles that send >90% of the Zr/Hf/Ti precursor to the exhaust, wafers rotate under a gas-bearing head. There, each precursor is confined by N2 curtains and pulled back through a cold-trap return loop for reuse.
why: Raises precursor utilization from ~5-10% to >50%, cutting hafnium/zirconium chemical and energy per wafer 5-10x and raising throughput 3-5x. Conformality in deep holes must be proven.

title: Arsenic-free n-type junctions via phosphorus epi and laser activation
idea: Combine source/drain formation with doping (zero masks): selective in-situ phosphorus-doped Si:P epi grows only on exposed Si, and nanosecond laser melt activates it, replacing arsenic implants and furnace spikes.
why: Removes arsine/arsenic (China-dominated) and toxic-gas handling; lower thermal budget saves energy and limits diffusion that worsens cell GIDL.

title: Size the capacitor for the median, the code for the tail
idea: Reverse the design target: cut capacitor aspect ratio from ~70:1 to ~20:1 so median cells still sense, and let the ~1% low-Cs or leaky tail cells be corrected by page-level ECC instead of building a taller pillar for the worst cell.
why: HAR etch/deposition time, fluorocarbon gas and support-nitride steps fall ~3x; fixes the capacitor charge wall in materials and capital rather than physics.

title: Brewed photoresists: fermentation-made fluorine-free photoacid generators
idea: Use engineered yeast and E. coli the way breweries and pharma ferment: make bio-based aromatic sulfonium cations, camphor- or lignin-derived sulfonic acid anions and chain-scission polymer backbones, giving ArF and KrF resists with no perfluoroalkyl sulfonate PAGs and no fluorinated surfactants.
why: PFAS PAGs and surfactants face restriction and come from a few Japanese suppliers; fermentation lines cost ~$10-50M rather than a large chemical plant and can be replicated anywhere, removing PFAS from the ~25-35 litho layers of a DRAM wafer.

title: Transcription cascade: roll-to-roll daughter stamps replace EUV array layers
idea: Cells copy DNA into many disposable mRNAs instead of reading the master directly. Write one e-beam master per periodic array layer, replicate it roll-to-roll into thousands of polymer daughter nanoimprint stamps, and imprint each wafer with a fresh daughter used only a few times before discarding it.
why: Disposable daughters solve nanoimprint's defect build-up and remove EUV (one supplier, ~$200M per tool) from 2-3 DRAM array layers with imprint tools costing ~1/10 as much.

title: High-pressure deuterium anneal trims the access-transistor leakage tail
idea: Box [standard cap | Si access with deuterium-passivated gate oxide and junction | standard | standard | Si | 10-20 atm D2 anneal at 400 C replacing Ar/forming-gas anneals]: Si-D bonds resist hot-carrier and thermal depassivation ~10x better than Si-H, so the trap sites behind trap-assisted GIDL stay passivated.
why: Leakage tail (13 fA) and refresh energy: pushing tail retention out 2-4x lets the refresh interval double or quadruple, roughly halving refresh power (16-33% of idle), using D2 rather than any rare gas.

title: Eliminate ceria CMP: flowable oxide plus atomic-layer etch-back planarization
idea: Replace ceria-slurry oxide CMP steps with spin-on polysilazane fill cured to SiO2, then planarize by quasi-atomic-layer etch-back that stops on a SiN etch-stop detected optically, so no slurry or pad is used.
why: Ceria abrasive is a rare-earth product dominated by China, and CMP is a top ultrapure-water and waste consumer; removes ~5-10 CMP steps per DRAM flow.

title: Microgram hydrogen backside gas replaces helium in every wafer chuck
idea: Kinetic theory: free-molecular gas-gap conductance scales ~P/sqrt(m), so H2 (m=2) moves ~1.4x more heat per Torr than He (m=4). An on-tool PEM electrolyzer feeds 5-10 Torr H2 into the ~1 cm3 chuck backside volume (~2 ug inventory, orders below any ignition hazard), with interlocked N2 purge.
why: Chuck backside cooling is a dominant fab helium use and Qatar (~30% of supply) has been offline since March 2026; removes He from etch/CVD chucks at near-zero consumable cost.

title: Electrochemical hydrogen pump recycles EUV scanner hydrogen
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: route each EUV scanner's source and collector hydrogen exhaust (hundreds of slm) through a tin trap and a proton-exchange electrochemical hydrogen pump. The pump compresses and purifies the H2 and returns it to the scanner feed, so the tool supplies most of its own hydrogen.
why: Cuts H2 purchase per scanner ~80% along with the energy to make it, lowers EUV operating cost, and frees hydrogen for helium substitution.

title: Substitute hydrogen for helium as backside wafer-cooling gas
idea: Etch and implant electrostatic chucks flow helium at 5-20 Torr behind each wafer; swap it for H2 (thermal conductivity ~0.18 vs ~0.15 W/m-K) at the same pressure, recirculated through an on-tool palladium purifier and diluted far below LEL with N2 ballast in the foreline; use an H2/Ne blend where hydrogen reactivity matters.
why: Helium is ~30% Qatar-sourced and offline since March 2026; backside cooling is one of the largest fab helium uses. Eliminates ~100% of that use while matching or improving wafer temperature uniformity.

title: Socketed design-for-disassembly DRAM packages for multi-life reuse
idea: Box [standard die | standard | standard | compression-interposer LGA packages on CAMM/CXL boards | n/a | solderless assembly]: standardize DRAM packages that mount without solder and carry an on-package wear/retention log, so dies move from retired boards to new controller generations.
why: Raises usable supply per fabbed bit: stretching DRAM service life from ~5 to ~10 years through reuse could halve new-bit demand for capacity tiers, with no solder-rework yield loss.

title: Grandmother saves the drippings: recapture fluorocarbon etch gases
idea: Persona: a grandmother who saves the bacon fat. Instead of burning C4F8, CF4 and NF3 in abatement, pass etch exhaust through a cold trap and fluorocarbon-selective membranes to recover >70%. Re-purify the gas by distillation at a regional plant and send the cylinders back.
why: Fluorocarbons are potent greenhouse gases, PFAS-adjacent and supply-limited. Recovery cuts purchases and CO2e by about half for the high-AR capacitor etch steps.

title: Tin can: indium- and gallium-free zinc-tin-oxide targets for gain cells
idea: Stimulus 'tin can' -> a 10-person team hot-presses Si-doped zinc-tin-oxide sputter targets from commodity ZnO and SnO2, tuned for BEOL oxide-semiconductor gain-cell transistors, so memory makers can skip IGZO's indium and gallium.
why: Gallium (~98% China, export-controlled) and indium (~60% China) become unnecessary for oxide-channel memory; target pressing is small-shop scale.

title: Micro-spring phonon chucks conduct wafer heat with no backside gas
idea: Scale jump from gas molecules to MEMS: the chuck face carries millions of ~10 um compliant SiC micro-springs that electrostatic clamping presses into solid contact. They carry ~500-1000 W/m2-K of heat by phonons, comparable to helium backside gas.
why: Removes helium (and hydrogen) from etch and deposition chucks entirely and ends gas-leak particle events. Wear and backside particles are the risk.

title: Indium- and gallium-free zinc-tin oxide gain cells under 350 C
idea: Effect: conduction through overlapping spherical Sn 5s / Zn 4s orbitals keeps amorphous Zn-Sn-O a good semiconductor, and its ~3.3 eV gap suppresses thermal generation to ~1e-19 A/um. Sputter ZTO at room temperature and anneal it at <=350 C to build 2T0C gain cells stacked in BEOL.
why: Scarce-element intensity of oxide memory: removes In (China ~60%) and Ga (China ~98%), with retention >100 s for ~1000x lower refresh energy.

title: Supercritical CO2 cleans and dries tall capacitors without ultrapure water
idea: Minify water and surface tension together: replace post-etch wet cleans and the UPW/IPA rinse-dry with supercritical CO2 plus a small co-solvent dose, so 70:1 pillars never feel capillary forces.
why: Cuts UPW draw for those steps ~90% and ends pillar leaning and collapse, which today cap aspect ratio and yield.

title: Delete the spare rows and fuses; the code is the repair
idea: Reverse post-fab repair: remove redundant rows/columns, laser/e-fuse banks and repair test flow from the die, and rely on page ECC sized for 1% BER to absorb defective cells.
why: Frees ~5-8% of die area and much ATE test time (tester capex, energy) per wafer.

title: Audio-RAM revival: sell partially defective DRAM for tolerant AI workloads
idea: Revive 1980s ARAM, defective DRAM sold for answering machines: bin HBM/DDR dies that fail full spec, burn their bad-row maps into on-die fuses/SPD, and sell them for error-tolerant KV cache and low-precision activation storage, with the OS/runtime retiring the mapped rows.
why: Scarce-resource intensity: HBM yield loss is 20-30%, and recovering half of it raises usable bits per wafer 10-15% with no new capacity.

title: Cu2O and SnO p-channel oxides put full CMOS periphery above arrays
idea: Effect: dispersive hole bands, from Cu 3d-O 2p hybridization in Cu2O and Sn 5s lone-pair mixing in SnO, give 1-5 cm2/Vs hole mobility. Sputtered at <=300 C and paired with n-type ZTO, they make complementary oxide decoders and drivers stacked over the array instead of beside it.
why: Periphery ~49% of die (fact 7): die area ~-35% and bits per wafer ~+50%, so less single-crystal Si (quartz, poly) per bit; Cu and Sn are abundant.

title: Colloidal-crystal capacitor holes, addressed after they form
idea: Reverse design-then-build: self-assemble a hexagonal monolayer of silica nanospheres as the capacitor-hole template (no lithography), accept ~1% vacancies and dislocations, and build a per-die address translation map after formation, the cell array following the crystal.
why: Removes EUV and immersion layers from capacitor patterning; nanosphere lithography uses abundant silica and cheap spin/dip coating tools.

title: Inductive chip-to-chip links stack memory dies without TSVs
idea: Minify vertical metal to zero: stack thinned memory dies and pass data through on-chip coil pairs (near-field inductive coupling), with power through edge wire bonds, eliminating TSVs, their copper fill and microbumps.
why: Removes HBM's TSV area and yield tax (fact 6), and leaves no solder joints to fatigue over 10 years at 125 C.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores as etch-free capacitor molds
idea: Effect: field-assisted ion migration during room-temperature aluminum anodization self-organizes hexagonal pores with aspect ratios >1000:1. A coarse nanoimprint pre-pattern registers them, and ALD TiN/dielectric/TiN at <=300 C fills them, so no high-AR plasma etch is needed. Every step stays below 400 C.
why: PFAS/fluorocarbon etch gases (C4F6, C4F8) and capital-heavy etchers; AR ~150:1 pushes Cs toward ~10 fF, breaking the capacitor wall (fact 1).

title: No-refresh DDR standard lets non-DRAM fabs supply main memory
idea: Inverts 'main memory is defined by the DRAM cell': publish a JEDEC-style NR-DDR/CXL interface with no refresh commands, fixed read/write windows and a nonvolatile-capable flag, so SiC, oxide, ferroelectric or magnetic dies from power, display and 200 mm fabs drop into existing sockets.
why: Zero refresh power by specification and new supply from underused US fabs without DRAM-specific capacitor tools; widens the supplier base beyond three companies.

title: Area-selective deposition grows features only where needed
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: use inhibitor monolayers (aminosilanes or small-molecule inhibitors) that block ALD on dielectric but not on metal. Landing-pad caps, contact liners and bitline spacers then self-align by growth instead of by litho + etch, deleting a resist coat, a fluorocarbon etch and a mask for each layer replaced.
why: Less PFAS-bearing resist and fluorinated greenhouse gas, and 1-2 fewer EUV/ArFi exposures per node, which lowers both capital and chemical intensity.

title: Catalytic-converter metal recovery: onsite tungsten hexafluoride regeneration loop
idea: Like precious-metal refiners that recover platinum from spent catalytic converters, trap unreacted WF6 and W-bearing byproducts in CVD exhaust, recover W from CMP slurry and chamber-clean residue, and directly fluorinate the recovered tungsten with onsite electrolytic F2 back into WF6 for the same tools.
why: Tungsten is ~80% Chinese and much of the WF6 fed to CVD never becomes film; a closed loop could cut virgin tungsten purchases ~50-70% and shrink HF/fluoride waste.

title: Solar PERC spatial ALD: atmospheric-pressure dielectrics at 10x throughput
idea: Solar lines deposit Al2O3 passivation by spatial ALD, moving wafers under separated precursor zones at atmospheric pressure. Build a bench spatial-ALD head in a university fab for ZrO2/Al2O3 capacitor and liner films, and measure precursor utilization and conformality in 10:1 trenches.
why: Conventional ALD wastes most of its precursor and needs vacuum; spatial ALD could cut Zr/Hf organometallic use, pump energy and tool capital per wafer ~2-5x.

title: Substitute zirconium silicate for hafnium oxide in periphery gates
idea: Replace HfO2 in DRAM periphery high-k metal gates with ALD Zr silicate, using silicon incorporation to suppress ZrO2 crystallization and an Al2O3 dipole layer for threshold tuning.
why: Hafnium is a costly byproduct of nuclear-grade zirconium refining with very few producers; Zr is ~50x more abundant and US/Australia-sourced.

title: Manganese-for-nickel stainless playbook: lanthanum replaces hafnium high-k
idea: Steelmakers swapped scarce nickel for manganese in 200-series stainless; swap hafnium in periphery high-k metal gates and capacitor interlayers for lanthanum aluminate and La-doped ZrO2, made from Mountain Pass (California) rare-earth output and deposited by ALD from lanthanum amidinates.
why: World hafnium supply is only ~70-100 t/yr from a few zirconium refiners; lanthanum is the most abundant rare earth with a domestic mine and separation, and LaAlO3 (k ~25) matches HfO2.

title: Anodized aluminum honeycomb becomes the capacitor scaffold
idea: Magnify nature's self-ordering: anodize a nanoimprint-seeded aluminum film into hexagonal alumina pores with aspect ratios above 300:1, line the pores with TiN/ZrO2/TiN by ALD, and hybrid-bond the capacitor sheet onto the access-transistor wafer.
why: A capacitor array with zero EUV layers and zero PFAS etch, made only from aluminum, acid and electricity; AR 300 gives ~4x the charge of today's pillars (fact 1).

title: Kraft-mill recovery cycle regenerates sulfuric acid and peroxide cleans
idea: Pulp mills recover more than 95% of their cooking chemicals in recovery boilers. Treat spent sulfuric-peroxide and SC1/SC2 baths the same way: boron-doped-diamond electrolysis regenerates persulfate and peroxide in-line, and vacuum distillation restores H2SO4 to semiconductor grade for reuse; no change to the DRAM product or DDR/HBM interface.
why: Cuts sulfuric-acid and peroxide purchases and neutralization waste ~70-80%, with associated UPW and trucking, easing water and chemical permits for U.S. fab siting.

title: Jeweler's bench-sweep recovery for sputter targets and chamber shields
idea: Jewelers recover gold dust from bench sweeps, while fabs scrap sputter targets at ~30-40% utilization and bead-blast metal off chamber shields into waste. Move to rotating cylindrical targets (>80% utilization) and send shield and target residues to closed-loop hydrometallurgy that recovers Ti, Ta, Co and W, with chain of custody back to the target makers.
why: Cuts virgin tantalum (conflict mineral), tungsten and cobalt per wafer ~2x.

title: Thyristor RAM fixed with delta-doped barriers that pin holding current
idea: T-RAM and Kilopass VLT died because the gated thyristor's holding current and standby leakage swung exponentially with temperature, forcing SOI and big guard-banding. Insert a planar-doped (delta-doped) triangular barrier in the p-base so a designed barrier height, not bulk diffusion, sets regeneration; this flattens holding current versus temperature and lets the vertical cell sit in plain bulk silicon with no germanium.
why: Capacitor- and nearly refresh-free 4F2 cell: no ZrO2/HfO2, no TiN pillars, no 60:1 capacitor etch gases; bulk instead of SOI halves crystal silicon per substrate; ~2x density and ~40% fewer high-AR etch steps per bit.

title: DIMM buffer deduplication magnifies effective capacity two to three times
idea: Magnify each physical bit's reach: a CXL/DIMM buffer chip hashes 64 B lines, stores identical and zero lines once in a content-addressed table, and compresses the rest with a ~4 ns LZ-lite engine.
why: Datacenter memory holds 20-60% duplicate or zero content. 2-3x effective GB per wafer means 2-3x less silicon, tungsten and hafnium per job.

title: U.S. Memories redone: take-or-pay offtake plus chokepoint-free bill of materials
idea: U.S. Memories Inc. (IBM, DEC, HP, Intel and others) died in 1990 when PC makers refused binding purchases once prices fell. Re-form it with 10-year take-or-pay contracts from hyperscalers, a price collar (floor and ceiling), and a charter requiring at least two non-chokepoint sources for every input (Mo for W, recaptured helium, non-Spruce-Pine crucibles).
why: The U.S. makes ~1-2% of DRAM; offtake de-risks a $15B+ fab while the material charter removes exposure to helium, quartz and tungsten shocks.

title: Nanocellulose build-up film replaces single-source ABF substrate dielectric
idea: Plant cell walls are cellulose microfibrils in a matrix, stiff and low-expansion. Cast roll-to-roll cellulose-nanofibril/bio-epoxy film (CTE ~5-10 ppm/K, close to silicon) with a silane moisture barrier as the build-up dielectric for DRAM and HBM package substrates.
why: Removes dependence on the near-monopoly Ajinomoto Build-up Film using wood pulp, and the low CTE cuts warpage, a major HBM and large-package yield loss.

title: Rotatable cylindrical targets and shield reclaim triple metal yield
idea: Magnify sputter-target utilization from ~30% to ~85%: move Ti, Mo, W and Ta PVD to rotating cylindrical cathodes, and recover metal from chamber shields by acid stripping and re-casting into new targets.
why: Cuts sputter-metal demand ~2.5x, including tantalum (a conflict mineral) and tungsten.

title: Memory consortium take-or-pay contracts open small U.S. helium fields
idea: Scale jump from the chamber to geology, and from monthly purchases to 15-year contracts. A U.S. memory consortium signs take-or-pay offtake from small Montana, Saskatchewan and Kansas helium fields equipped with modular membrane-plus-PSA wellhead units, with delivery as liquid helium in ISO containers.
why: Hedges the Qatar ~30% outage and stabilizes fab helium cost. These small fields are uneconomic without an anchor buyer.

title: Molecular-monolayer doping replaces arsine, phosphine and ion implanters
idea: A junction needs ~1e13-1e15 dopant atoms/cm2, roughly one molecular monolayer; graft phosphonate or boronate monolayers from solution with dose set by ligand footprint, cap with oxide and spike-anneal. It is conformal, so it dopes 3D sidewalls that implanters cannot reach.
why: Removes toxic, concentrated dopant gases (AsH3, PH3, B2H6) and ~100+ kW implanters per tool, and enables doping of buried 3D tiers.

title: Fab load-shifting using UPW and liquid nitrogen as energy storage
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action: run the power-hungry subsystems that can be buffered (ASU liquefaction, UPW reverse osmosis, chiller ice making) in pulses during cheap renewable or nuclear hours. Their output is stored in LN2 dewars, UPW tanks and ice banks, so grid draw is periodic while the process tools run continuously.
why: Energy intensity: ~15-25% of fab load becomes flexible, for ~10% lower energy cost and access to U.S. sites with weaker grids.

title: Electrolytically regenerated persulfate replaces sulfuric-peroxide wet strip
idea: TRIZ #38 Strong oxidants: replace single-pass SPM (H2SO4 + H2O2) resist strip and organic clean with an electrolyzed-sulfuric loop. Boron-doped-diamond anodes continuously regenerate peroxodisulfate from the same acid, so it is recirculated instead of drained.
why: Cuts sulfuric acid and peroxide purchase, neutralization chemicals and rinse water ~80-90%, which simplifies chemical logistics for new U.S. sites.

title: Square-meter laser interference lithography for perfectly periodic memory arrays
idea: Ideal: one flash of light patterns a whole panel. Closest: two- or three-beam interference of a 266/213 nm solid-state laser writes periodic lines or hexagonal dots (pitch >=0.12 um) over Gen-8 panels or R2R webs in seconds with no reticle or projection optics; only periphery and staircases use cheap panel steppers.
why: 100x: memory arrays are periodic, so they need no imaging optics; tool capex per m2 is ~1000x below EUV, enabling the ~0.25 um-F panel/foil tiers needed for ~$0.1/GB. Trades 5-10x larger F and stitching/overlay risk.

title: Retired server DIMMs reharvested into pooled CXL memory
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round, memory flowing back up the supply chain: hyperscalers return DDR4/DDR5 from decommissioned servers to a qualification line. The line desolders the DRAM, retests it at speed and temperature, bins it by retention class, and rebuilds it onto CXL Type-3 expander cards for capacity tiers.
why: Adds usable DRAM supply with zero wafers, at ~30-50% of the cost per bit of new parts. A large share of retired server DRAM is still functional.

title: Low-E glass tin oxide templates high-k rutile capacitor dielectric
idea: Architectural low-E and solar glass is coated with fluorine-doped tin oxide, a conductive rutile-structure oxide. Use ALD F:SnO2 or Sb:SnO2 as the storage-node electrode liner so TiO2 nucleates directly in the rutile phase (k ~80-100) below 400 C, replacing ZrO2/HfO2 stacks (k ~40) and the Ru electrodes normally needed for rutile templating.
why: Fact 1 says more charge needs k ~70; doubling k gives ~2x Cs or ~40% shorter pillars (less HAR etch) using only Sn, Ti and O, with no hafnium or ruthenium.

title: Diatom biosilicification: room-temperature catalytic silica for gapfill and supports
idea: Diatoms build intricate silica shells at ambient temperature using polyamine/silaffin peptides that catalyze silicic-acid condensation. Use synthetic polyamine-catalyzed silica sols to conformally fill capacitor support lattices and shallow trenches below 100 C with a gentle cure, replacing high-temperature furnace TEOS and polysilazane steam anneals.
why: Cuts furnace energy and quartz furnace-ware wear for dielectric fill; the low thermal budget also protects TiN/high-k capacitor stacks, allowing higher-k phases.

title: Let the crystal draw the lines: vicinal step templates
idea: Rearrange mask and substrate: use miscut silicon annealed into regularly bunched atomic steps at a set pitch, then selectively oxidize step edges to template wordline pitch without printing it with EUV.
why: Removes one or more EUV layers (single-supplier tool, ~55% of wafer cost is depreciation) by letting the lattice provide the pitch for free.

title: Chlor-alkali cells on site: electrolytic ozone water replaces sulfuric-peroxide cleans
idea: Chlor-alkali plants make chemicals from brine with electricity; put diamond-electrode electrolyzers at each wet bench to generate ozonated water, hydrogen water and peroxide on demand, replacing piranha resist strips and RCA cleans.
why: Removes bulk semiconductor-grade sulfuric acid and H2O2 (short in the U.S. in 2021-22), their trucking and neutralization waste, and cuts chemical and rinse water ~30-50% using only domestic water and electricity.

title: Self-barrier copper-manganese bitlines from Arizona copper
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero tungsten and zero TiN on the bitline. Deposit a Cu-0.5%Mn alloy into the bitline trench; on anneal the Mn migrates to the dielectric and forms a ~1-2 nm MnSiOx self-barrier, so nearly the whole cross-section is copper.
why: Copper (~1.7 uOhm-cm bulk vs W ~5.6) lets bitlines run longer with fewer sense amps, attacking the 49% periphery share, while dropping a China-concentrated metal.

title: IBM racetrack fixed with grain-free amorphous iron-boron wires on glass
idea: IBM's racetrack memory stalled because domain walls pinned on edge roughness and grain boundaries, and stacks needed Pt/Co/Ni multilayers. Sputter amorphous Fe80B20 (metglas chemistry, no grains) nanowires on fusion-drawn display glass with sub-0.3 nm roughness, shift in-plane walls by spin-transfer current pulses, and read at one end of each wire.
why: Stores 10-100 bits per access device, cutting transistors and periphery per bit; no Co, Pt, Ir or Ru; Fe and B are abundant; nonvolatile, so no refresh; shift latency suits streaming tiers.

title: Substitute fab-heat membrane distillation for fresh-water intake
idea: Route RO reject and rinse effluent through membrane-distillation modules heated by 40-70 C process-cooling return water, polish the distillate back to UPW, and crystallize the brine for zero liquid discharge.
why: Raises site water recovery from ~60% to >95%, cutting fresh intake >10x using waste heat rather than extra electricity.

title: Pharma flow chemistry: fab-side microreactors brew ALD precursors
idea: Pharma replaced batch kettles with continuous-flow microreactors; synthesize Zr, Hf, Mo and Al ALD precursors beside the fab from Oregon zirconium and hafnium chlorides and Gulf Coast amines in skid-scale flow reactors with inline distillation, delivered by pipe instead of shipped cylinders.
why: Precursors come from a handful of Korean, Japanese and European firms; point-of-use flow synthesis gives a domestic supply, cuts inventory and cylinder logistics, and delivers fresher, purer precursor.

title: Substitute hydrocarbon dielectric fluids for PFAS heat-transfer fluids
idea: Swap perfluoropolyether and fluoroketone fluids in etch-chamber chillers and burn-in/test handlers for hydrogenated polyalphaolefin or synthetic isoparaffin fluids rated -40 to +150 C, run in nitrogen-blanketed sealed reservoirs to manage flammability.
why: 3M exited PFAS manufacturing at end-2025; removes a supply chokepoint and regulatory risk with fluids ~10x cheaper per liter.

title: ALD exhaust cold-trap reclaims precursors for on-site repurification
idea: Combine the ALD foreline trap with a precursor refinery: a staged cryogenic trap captures the >90% of Zr/Hf/Ti metal-organic precursor that passes unreacted during purge pulses, and an on-site fractional distillation unit repurifies it to 6N for re-feed.
why: Cuts metal precursor consumption 3-5x and abatement energy; the capacitor stack burns the most ALD cycles in the fab.

title: Short-mean-free-path NiAl intermetallic buried wordlines replace tungsten
idea: Scale jump from bulk metal to the 10 nm wire: at buried-wordline widths, resistivity depends on the electron mean free path more than on the bulk value. B2 intermetallics such as NiAl or CoAl (mean free path ~5 nm vs ~16 nm for W) therefore match or beat W. Deposit Ni/Al ALD nanolaminates into the recessed trench, anneal them to the ordered B2 phase, and use a thin AlN liner instead of a TiN barrier.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) from the densest metal layer of the array. Projected 10-30% lower line resistance below 15 nm width, allowing longer wordlines and fewer drivers in the periphery.

title: Talk through the stack, not drill it: inductive die coupling
idea: Rearrange vertical connection from metal to field: stack thinned DRAM dies that exchange data by on-chip inductive coils (wireless near-field links) instead of copper TSVs.
why: Removes Cu/Ta/Ti TSV metallization and the TSV keep-out area behind the ~3x HBM wafer-area tax; could cut HBM wafer area per bit ~30%.

title: DNA-origami masks pattern sub-10 nm capacitor arrays without EUV
idea: Box [ZrO2 cap | Si access | voltage SA | standard | Si | DNA-origami self-assembly on coarse docking sites + silica mineralization]: dock origami tiles carrying a programmed honeycomb of 8 nm openings onto DUV-defined sites, mineralize them with DNA-templated sol-gel silica into a hard mask, and transfer the hole array into the capacitor mold.
why: EUV single supplier and 5-7 EUV layers: replaces 2-3 capacitor/contact EUV layers with room-temperature biochemistry; DNA synthesis cost has fallen by orders of magnitude.

title: Lateral-line sensor tape maps helium leaks along every gas line
idea: Fish sense flow along the body with a lateral line of tiny neuromasts. Print a tape of thermal-conductivity microheater sensors every 5 cm (helium conducts heat ~6x better than air) with printed NFC readout, and wrap it along gas sticks, VCR fittings and chuck feeds to locate helium leaks in real time.
why: Leaks and over-flows are a large share of fab helium loss; continuous mapping could cut it 10-20% for a few dollars per metre.

title: Hermit-crab re-shelling: retired DDR4 rehoused in CXL expanders
idea: Hermit crabs move into shells that others discard. Buy DDR4 DIMMs from server decommissioning, screen them with a 24-hour retention and row-hammer test, and resell them inside CXL Type-3 expander cards with DDR4 controllers as a warm memory tier.
why: Recovers exabytes of working DRAM that would otherwise be shredded, adding supply in weeks with no wafers, helium or quartz at perhaps 20-30% of new DDR5 cost per GB.

title: Ugly-produce partial-good DRAM dies with fused-out banks
idea: Adapted from grocers selling cosmetically imperfect produce. Bin DRAM dies that have dead banks or subarrays, which are normally scrapped, as partial-good parts: on-die fuses remap the address space, an SPD field reports usable capacity, and OS/CXL memory managers consume the odd-sized capacities.
why: Recovers ~3-8% of wafer output at advanced nodes. Each recovered bit already carries its full embedded helium, quartz, tungsten and energy, so it comes at zero extra resource.

title: Hafnium-, zirconium-, ruthenium-free CaTiO3 capacitors on MoO2 electrodes
idea: Ideal: a capacitor made from limestone and common metals. Closest: ALD perovskite CaTiO3 (bulk k~170) or Al-doped rutile TiO2 grown on a rutile-structured MoO2 bottom electrode that templates the high-k phase at <=400 C, replacing RuO2/Ru electrodes and ZrO2/HfO2 stacks.
why: Fact 1 asks for k~70: k>=80 could cut required capacitor AR from ~70 to ~40 while removing Zr/Hf (zircon byproducts) and Ru (South Africa ~90%); leakage is the open risk.

title: Eliminate ultrapure-water rinses: supercritical CO2 cleans that stop pillar collapse
idea: Replace wet clean, rinse and IPA dry after capacitor-mold strip and post-etch steps with supercritical CO2 plus small co-solvent doses, recompressing and reusing >95% of the CO2.
why: Zero surface tension ends capillary collapse of 60-75:1 pillars, allowing AR~100+ capacitors (fact 1), and removes a large share of UPW per wafer.

title: Dry-cleaner wafer benches run on ethanol-plant CO2
idea: Dry cleaners wash clothes in liquid CO2 without water; replace post-etch residue removal and rinse-dry steps with supercritical CO2 plus co-solvent chambers, fed by fermentation CO2 captured at Midwest ethanol plants and recycled in a closed loop.
why: Cuts ultrapure water and IPA on cleaning steps ~50-80%, prevents pattern collapse of 70:1 capacitors, and turns a domestic waste gas into a process fluid.

title: Substitute ordinary US quartzite for Spruce Pine pegmatite via chlorination
idea: Upgrade widespread domestic quartzite and glass sand to crucible grade: microwave thermal-shock decrepitation opens fluid inclusions, hot Cl2/HCl gas leaching at 1100-1200 C volatilizes Al, alkali and Fe as chlorides, and vacuum fusion yields bubble-free high-purity silica.
why: Breaks the single-district HPQ chokepoint for crucibles, furnace ware and mask blanks by turning dozens of common US deposits into feedstock.

title: All-carbon capacitor mold etched with oxygen instead of fluorocarbons
idea: Combine mold material and strip chemistry: replace the oxide/nitride capacitor mold with amorphous carbon, etch holes in O2/N2/COS plasma with sulfur sidewall passivation, deposit electrodes, then remove the mold in the same O2 ash rather than an HF wet strip.
why: Removes C4F6/C4F8/CHF3 (high-GWP, PFAS-adjacent) from DRAM's hardest etch and the HF strip; dry removal ends pillar collapse; carbon etches 2-3x faster, so fewer etch tools.

title: Carbon molds etched by oxygen with sulfur sidewall passivation
idea: Periodic-table walk, C+S (6,16): form capacitor holes in an amorphous-carbon mold using O2 plasma with COS/SO2 additive, whose sulfur-carbon sidewall film replaces fluorocarbon polymer passivation for straight ~80:1 holes; after electrode deposition the mold is simply ashed in O2.
why: Removes C4F8/CHF3 and HF mold strip; ashing instead of a wet release avoids pillar collapse and rinse water.

title: Bring the fab to the helium: co-locate on U.S. gas fields
idea: Reverse siting logic: place the next U.S. DRAM fab beside helium-rich gas processing (Wyoming/Kansas) and firm nuclear/hydro power, with direct pipeline helium and on-site recapture.
why: Shields from the Qatar outage and makes helium a local input; improves U.S. manufacturability through cheap firm power and supply security.

title: LNG terminal cold energy runs fab nitrogen and chillers
idea: Adapted from Japanese LNG import terminals, which use regasification cold (-162 C) to power air separation and cold storage. Site a fab beside a US regas terminal (e.g. Cove Point, Elba Island, Everett) and drive its nitrogen air-separation unit and process chillers from LNG cold through an intermediate loop.
why: Nitrogen generation and chillers are a large share of a fab's energy load. LNG cold cuts ASU electricity ~50% and chiller power ~30%.

title: Fiber-laser 193 nm sources end the neon dependence
idea: Minify rare-gas use to zero: replace ArF excimer lasers (neon buffer gas, historically ~50% from Ukraine and Russia) with Yb-fiber lasers frequency-converted to 193 nm in nonlinear-crystal cascades for DUV scanners.
why: Removes the neon and fluorine-gas chokepoints and raises wall-plug efficiency; DUV prints most DRAM layers.

title: Electromagnetic cold-crucible Czochralski eliminates the quartz crucible
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution (a field replaces the vessel): hold the melt in a segmented water-cooled copper crucible where induction currents heat and partly levitate it inside a frozen silicon skull, so silicon touches only silicon. Gettering oxygen is added deliberately through O2/H2O partial pressure, and nitrogen doping restores wafer strength.
why: Removes the HPQ crucible chokepoint (Spruce Pine >80%) and crucible-borne metal contamination, using only Si, Cu, O and N.

title: Pearl-oyster self-crucible: silicon melt held in its own frozen skin
idea: An oyster seals an irritant inside its own nacre. Grow Cz ingots in a segmented, water-cooled cold crucible with electromagnetic levitation, so the melt touches only a frozen skull of its own silicon and never quartz.
why: Eliminates high-purity quartz crucibles (Spruce Pine >80%) and lowers oxygen in the crystal; the higher RF energy is offset by a reusable crucible and recycled skull.

title: Hot-swap chamber liner cassettes eliminate NF3 in-situ cleans
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero NF3 or fluorinated chamber-clean gas. Build ALD/CVD chamber walls from robot-swappable liner cassettes; after N wafers, swap in a fresh cassette in minutes and strip the dirty one offline in a closed-loop alkaline electrochemical bath that recovers the TiN and ZrO2 deposits.
why: In-situ NF3 cleans are a top fab greenhouse emission and a fluorochemical dependency; this removes them, recovers Zr, and raises uptime because clean-and-season cycles vanish.

title: Iron-nitride magnetic tunnel junction RAM free of platinum-group metals
idea: Minify rare metals: replace MRAM's CoFeB/Pt/Ir/Ru/Ta stack with strained tetragonal Fe16N2 free and pinned layers, an MgO barrier and an Fe-Mn synthetic antiferromagnet, keeping thermal stability above 80 kT at 125 C.
why: Byte-addressable working memory with 1e12+ endurance built only from Fe, N, Mg, O and Mn; removes platinum-group metals and cobalt while meeting 10-year retention at 125 C.

title: Optical-fiber soot deposition makes synthetic-silica crucible inner walls
idea: Adapted from outside vapor deposition (OVD) used to make optical-fiber preforms. SiCl4-derived silica soot is deposited on a rotating crucible-shaped mandrel and sintered into a 3-5 mm fully synthetic inner layer. That layer is backed with ordinary lower-grade fused silica, so no Spruce Pine HPQ ever touches the melt.
why: Breaks the >80% Spruce Pine high-purity quartz chokepoint. SiCl4 is a cheap polysilicon by-product, and a synthetic liner lowers metal contamination and may lengthen crucible life.

title: Bacterial magnetite crystals as uniform nonvolatile bit cells
idea: Inverts 'memory materials are deposited by vacuum tools': harvest monodisperse ~45 nm magnetite crystals grown by magnetotactic bacteria in water at room temperature, self-assemble them onto chemically patterned sites as magnetic bits, and write and read them with crossed current lines and a Hall-sensor stripe.
why: Nonvolatile, so zero refresh; fermentation and iron replace sputtered Co/Pt stacks, and biological size uniformity removes the bit-to-bit spread that limits magnetic memory.

title: Template-stabilized rutile titania reaches k near 100 without hafnium
idea: Effect: rutile TiO2 has k ~80-170 but normally forms low-k anatase. ALD it onto a lattice-matched rutile-structure conductor (Sb:SnO2 or MoO2 instead of scarce Ru) so epitaxial templating locks in rutile, and use Al doping at grain boundaries to plug leakage.
why: Capacitor charge wall (needs k~70) and Zr/Hf dependence: ~2x Cs at the same aspect ratio, or AR cut from ~70 to ~35, which also cuts fluorocarbon etch time; Ti is the 9th most abundant element.

title: Photo-electrochemical planarization ends dependence on ceria slurries
idea: Worsen: make every oxide CMP step consume Chinese rare-earth ceria slurry and polyurethane pads. Flip: planarize by UV-activated photo-electrochemical etching in a thin electrolyte film under a TiO2-coated transparent platen. High points see more field and light and dissolve faster, so no abrasive is needed.
why: Rare-earth (Ce) chokepoint, slurry waste water and scratch defects: no ceria or abrasive slurry at all.

title: Prefab-housing utility cores: periphery wafers from mature U.S. logic fabs
idea: Modular housing builds the plumbing and electrical core in a factory and drops it on site. Split DRAM into an array wafer (DRAM fab) and a periphery CMOS wafer built on 28-40 nm logic lines at U.S. foundries with spare capacity, then hybrid-bond them face-to-face; the bonded die presents the same DDR5/HBM pins and timing.
why: Periphery is ~49% of the die (fact 7) and needs no EUV; moving it to depreciated mature fabs frees ~40% of DRAM-fab wafer capacity and raises bits per DRAM wafer.

title: Cleanroom-free fab: wafers ride sealed nitrogen tunnels between tools
idea: Inverts 'the whole fab must be an ISO-class cleanroom': wafers stay permanently inside sealed N2-purged carriers that dock to sealed tools through an overhead N2/vacuum tunnel network, so the building itself is ordinary ISO-8 air and HVAC moves ~10x less air.
why: Cleanroom HVAC and makeup air are ~30-50% of fab electricity and drive humidification water; lowers shell capital and build time, easing US siting.

title: Hydrogen-ambient Czochralski pulling in silicon-nitride crucibles
idea: Box [standard | standard | standard | standard | 300 mm CZ Si under recycled low-pressure H2 | Si3N4-coated SiC crucible + magnetic CZ]: sweep SiO and CO from the puller with H2 instead of argon (its higher thermal conductivity allows faster pulling) and hold the melt in a nitride-faced crucible that releases nitrogen, useful for void control, rather than oxygen.
why: Removes both the argon purge and the Spruce Pine HPQ crucible from wafer making; H2 heat extraction might raise pull rate ~10-20%.

title: Porous-silicon template wafers spawn fifty epitaxial DRAM wafers each
idea: Scale shift from the 775 um wafer to the ~5 um a DRAM array actually uses. Anodize a reusable CZ template to form a double-porosity seam, grow 10-20 um of epitaxial Si on it, bond to a low-grade carrier, and lift off along the seam. Re-polish the template and reuse it 50 or more times.
why: Cuts prime CZ silicon and high-purity quartz crucible use per DRAM wafer by ~10-50x. Oxygen-lean epi silicon may also tighten the retention-leakage tail.

title: Johnsen-Rahbek solid-contact chucks remove backside gas entirely
idea: Effect: the Johnsen-Rahbek effect concentrates the clamping field across micro-gaps of a slightly conductive dielectric, giving ~10x the clamp force of a Coulomb chuck. Pair it with a compliant AlN-nanocomposite top layer so heat leaves through >30% real solid contact area instead of gas, and tune temperature uniformity with zoned JR voltages.
why: Helium: eliminates the backside-gas loop and its leak points; contact conductance >1000 W/m2K, comparable to He-gas cooling at the ~10 Torr typical of etch tools.

title: One block mask lets capacitor ZrO2 double as periphery gate
idea: Combine the cell-capacitor ZrO2 ALD with the periphery high-k gate: periphery moves to a gate-last module whose trenches are opened by the single added mask, so the same ZrO2 run coats capacitor and periphery gates, with La/Al dipoles setting Vt.
why: Removes hafnium entirely and one full HKMG dielectric module (~6-8 steps); ALD tool demand per wafer start down ~10%.

title: Molten calcium chloride electrolysis turns ordinary sand into silicon
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ca+Cl (20,17): electro-deoxidize pressed SiO2 pellets from ordinary sand at ~850 C in molten CaCl2 (FFC route), with the salt recycled, and feed the Si powder to zone refining and CZ recharge.
why: Bypasses the arc furnace (11-13 kWh/kg plus coke) and Siemens chlorosilane steps; any sand works, no fluorides, U.S.-sited.
